items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: To name a few, there was Billy Taylor... Hopkins tenor man and the great Coleman Hawkins as well as Benny Carter.

ctx.x: To name a few, there was Billy Taylor, the bass player, his son Billy, Jr., who also played bass, John Brown, a bass player, Jonah Jones, the ex-Stuff Smith and Cab Calloway trumpet man, Doles Dicksens, bass, Slick Jones, drummer on many Fats Waller recordings, Al Hall, bass, Gus Askins, trumpet, Leonard "Henn" Davis, trumpet, Bobby Sands, ex-Claude
Hopkins tenor man and the great Coleman Hawkins as well as Benny Carter.

The Golden Gate closed and the band worked a few weeks at the Savoy. Benny engaged Vic Dickenson in the bone section. He had been in Count Basie's band and told me that Besie had told him to take a rest because he was hitting the bottle too heavy and his playing was getting a little too sluggish. But within two weeks, Basie recalled Vic and he left Benny which Benny knew would happen. But Benny and the rest of the gang enjoyed listening to Vic for the short while he was with us.
